title: NASA SBIR/STTR Phase I
description: Phase I R&D awards for small businesses working on NASA technology subtopics, now released as appendices under a BAA valid through Sept 2027. Recurring: the 2026 A/B appendices closed May 21, 2026 and further appendices are expected but not yet posted.
eligibility: U.S. small business (500 or fewer employees); STTR requires a research institution partner

title: DoW SBIR 26.BX Release 6 (SpaceWERX space topics)
agency: U.S. Space Force / SpaceWERX (Department of the Air Force)
description: Release 6 of the Department of War SBIR solicitation, including Space Force topics such as tactical awareness payloads for agile satellites, space cyber, and on-orbit logistics. Offers Phase I and Direct-to-Phase II awards.
eligibility: U.S. for-profit small business (500 or fewer employees); PI primarily employed by the company

title: DoW STTR 26.TX Release 6 (SpaceWERX space topics)
agency: U.S. Space Force / SpaceWERX (Department of the Air Force)
description: STTR companion to Release 6, including a Space Force topic on space domain operational environment assessment. Small business must team with a research institution.
eligibility: U.S. small business partnered with a research institution (40% business / 30% institution minimum)

title: DARPA STTR: Fuel-Flexible Spacecraft Electric Propulsion System (DPA26TZ06-DV005)
description: Direct-to-Phase II STTR to build a spacecraft electric propulsion system that runs efficiently on air, water, CO2 mixes, or ammonia/hydrazine-derived gases. $1M base plus $1M option over 24 months.
eligibility: U.S. small business with research institution partner; must show Phase I-equivalent prior work

title: SpaceWERX TACFI (PY26.2)
agency: U.S. Space Force / SpaceWERX (Department of the Air Force)
description: Tactical Funding Increase that adds government money, matched by private or government funds, to scale Space Force and Air Force SBIR/STTR Phase II technologies toward transition. Continuous rolling submissions.
eligibility: Small business on an active or completed DAF SBIR/STTR Phase II, with matching funds and a government partner

title: SpaceWERX STRATFI
agency: U.S. Space Force / SpaceWERX (Department of the Air Force)
description: Strategic Funding Increase for larger Phase II-to-Phase III scale-ups with required private and government matching. Recurring annual program-year cycle; no STRATFI window is open as of verification (only PY26.2 TACFI is).
eligibility: DAF SBIR/STTR Phase II performers with matching private investment and government sponsor

title: NSF SBIR/STTR Phase I (America's Seed Fund)
description: Non-dilutive Phase I funding for deep-tech startups across fields including space technology. A Project Pitch invitation is required first; next full-proposal deadline Nov 4, 2026, then Mar 4, 2027 and Jul 7, 2027.
eligibility: U.S. small business (500 or fewer employees) with an invited Project Pitch; PI at least 51% employed by the company

title: NSF SBIR/STTR Phase II
description: Follow-on funding of up to $1.25M over about 24 months for NSF Phase I awardees to advance toward commercialization. Recurs three times a year.
eligibility: Prior NSF SBIR/STTR Phase I awardees

title: NSF SBIR/STTR Fast-Track
description: Combined Phase I and Phase II proposal ($400K Phase I plus $1.155M Phase II) for startups ready to move quickly. Requires an invited Project Pitch.
eligibility: U.S. small business with an invited Project Pitch

title: NASA TechLeap Prize: Orbital Clarity Challenge
description: Prize for low-cost, scalable payloads that measure thermospheric density, pressure, or drag in low Earth orbit. Up to four winners share up to $500K each across three phases plus a free orbital test flight; registration closes Oct 28, 2026.
eligibility: U.S. teams per NASA prize rules

title: NASA TechRise Student Challenge 2026-27
description: Student teams design experiments to fly on NASA-sponsored commercial suborbital flights. Winners get $1,000 and a flight slot.
eligibility: Grades 6-12 student teams at U.S. schools, led by an educator

title: Army xTech|Search 10
description: The Army's flagship open-topic prize competition for dual-use tech. Up to $1M in cash prizes (up to $200K first place) plus a path for finalists to Army SBIR/STTR awards of up to $300K.
eligibility: U.S. for-profit small business (500 or fewer employees), majority U.S.-owned

title: Arizona Innovation Challenge (Fall 2026)
description: $100K non-dilutive award plus three months of support for early-stage Arizona startups; the Fall 2026 cycle is focused on SaaS and AI companies (space software firms qualify). Recurs each cycle with rotating sector focus.
eligibility: Arizona early-stage SaaS/AI startups; revenue band roughly $5K-$50K MRR

title: AZ FAST Grant (SBIR/STTR proposal support)
description: Small grants that pay for an approved consultant to help Arizona companies prepare a federal SBIR/STTR Phase I proposal. Recurring; the last verified round (Nov 2025) funded up to $3,000 per company and a new round date was not confirmed on the official page.
eligibility: Arizona-based small businesses with high-risk, high-tech SBIR-suitable technology

title: Arizona Competes Fund
description: Discretionary deal-closing grants to attract, expand, or retain basic enterprises creating quality jobs in Arizona, plus programs for small, rural, and micro businesses. Awarded case by case, not by open call.
eligibility: Companies expanding or locating in Arizona that create jobs at or above median county wage

title: Arizona State Trade Expansion Program (AZSTEP)
description: Helps Arizona small businesses cover costs of entering or expanding into export markets, such as trade shows, export training, and website localization. Useful for aerospace suppliers selling abroad.
eligibility: Arizona small businesses entering or expanding export markets

title: Arizona Space Grant Space Industry Internship Program
description: Places student interns at small and mid-sized Arizona space companies with stipends paid by the consortium, not the company ($1,000 per month for 10 hours a week). Recurring: industry applications for 2026-27 ran Aug 3-14, 2026.
eligibility: Small to mid-sized Arizona space companies (hosts); students at affiliated Arizona institutions

title: Arizona Space Grant Graduate Fellowship
description: Up to six fellowships a year for University of Arizona STEM graduate students, covering tuition plus a stipend of at least $15,000. Recurring annually; the AY2026-27 deadline was April 13, 2026.
eligibility: STEM graduate students at the University of Arizona

title: ASU Venture Devils Demo Day Seed Grants
agency: Arizona State University (J. Orin Edson Entrepreneurship + Innovation Institute)
description: Non-dilutive seed grants of $1K-$20K awarded at twice-yearly Demo Days (December and April) from a pool of over $400K. Recurring.
eligibility: ASU-affiliated startups enrolled in Venture Devils

title: NOAA SBIR (FY2027)
description: Annual SBIR funding for products tied to NOAA's mission, including satellite, weather, and Earth-observation tech. NOAA says the FY27 cycle launches in fall 2026; dates and amounts not yet posted.
eligibility: U.S. small businesses with NOAA-mission tech that has commercial uses

title: AFRL STAR-FISH: Secure by Design Space Vehicle (BAA FA9453-21-S-0001)
agency: Air Force Research Laboratory, Space Vehicles Directorate
description: Two-step BAA for cyber-hardened space vehicle R&D: flat-sat design, cyber-hardening software, and ground and on-orbit demos. About $14M total across FY2027-2030; white papers due Oct 11-12, 2026 (sources differ, confirm on SAM.gov).
eligibility: U.S. entities; U.S. citizen personnel, Secret clearance anticipated, ITAR compliance, no foreign-owned primes

title: DIU Commercial Solutions Opening (space Areas of Interest)
description: DIU posts Areas of Interest (recent space ones include laser comms, space manufacturing, and space threat intelligence) and awards fast prototype Other Transaction agreements from short solution briefs. Recurring; the latest space AOI closed Sept 24, 2026.
eligibility: Commercial companies of any size, including non-traditional defense contractors

title: NASA Early Stage Innovations (ESI)
description: University grants for early-stage space technology research, around 24 awards per year of at least $750K. Recurring annually; the 2026 preliminary proposals closed Aug 13, 2026 (invited full proposals due Dec 16, 2026).
eligibility: U.S. universities; PI must be tenured or tenure-track faculty

title: NASA Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) Phase I
description: Funds visionary early-stage aerospace concepts. Recurring annually; the most recent cycle had about 12 awards of at least $175K, with Step A proposals usually due in July.
eligibility: Open to most U.S. organizations, including companies and universities

title: NASA Space Technology Graduate Research Opportunities (NSTGRO)
description: Grants to universities for graduate students doing space technology research. Annual; the last solicitation closed Jan 29, 2026 and the next is expected on NSPIRES.
eligibility: U.S. citizens or permanent residents in master's or PhD programs at accredited U.S. universities

title: NASA ROSES-2026 (Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences)
description: NASA's main annual umbrella solicitation for space and Earth science research, with dozens of program elements. ROSES-2026 is pending release (planned July 2026, not yet published as of verification).
eligibility: Universities, nonprofits, companies, and NASA centers depending on program element

title: Colorado Advanced Industries Early-Stage Capital and Retention Grant
agency: Colorado Office of Economic Development and International Trade
description: Up to $250K (up to $500K for multi-industry projects) for Colorado tech companies, including aerospace, commercializing products made in Colorado. Requires 2:1 matching; recurring, the last cycle closed Aug 27, 2026.
eligibility: Colorado companies with under $10M revenue and under $20M raised; 2:1 match required

title: Colorado Advanced Industries Proof of Concept Grant
agency: Colorado Office of Economic Development and International Trade
description: Up to $150K for Colorado research institutions to speed applied research toward commercialization in advanced industries including aerospace. Recurring; the last cycle closed Aug 27, 2026.
eligibility: Colorado research institutions; 1:3 matching required

title: Space Florida-Israel Innovation Partnership
description: Annual joint call funding Florida-Israel company pairs developing aerospace technology, about $2M per year in total. Recurring; the 2026 call closed Feb 16, 2026 and the next call typically opens in the fall.
eligibility: Teams pairing a Florida company with an Israeli company

title: Planetary Society STEP Grants
description: Donor-funded grants for projects on exploring other worlds, finding life, and planetary defense. Awarded about every two years; the latest winners were announced Sept 2026, so the next round is expected around 2028.
eligibility: Open internationally to universities, companies, and individuals
